summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for July 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

eli5.summary: It is like a monthly count of how many cars used each road, written down so people can see which roads are busy.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in july 1973
which host sent the most packets in july 1973
subtitle: BBN's July 1973 count of packets sent by each ARPANET Host, split into internode and intranode traffic.

tldr.problem: The network community wanted regular figures on how much traffic each Host put onto the ARPANET.
tldr.mechanism: A table lists, per Host, packets output within the same node (intranode) and to other nodes (internode), with totals and an average daily internode figure over 31 days.
tldr.outcome: Overall, 83499220 internode and 58210780 intranode packets were output, at 1.04 packets per message.

today: RFC 556 is a monthly statistics memo that updates RFC 538. Its metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content: RFC 556, by A. McKenzie of BBN-NET and dated 13 August 1973, encloses the Host traffic statistics for July 1973. It updates RFC 538 and is a data memo that defines no protocol.
sections.eli5: A short note hands over the July scoreboard.

sections.title: The Host Throughput Table
sections.content:
The table is titled Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). For each site, each Host number has INTER-NODE packets (to other nodes), INTRA-NODE packets (within the node) and a TOTAL. Sites with several Hosts get a subtotal row with the average daily internode figure and the number of days, 31 for every listed site.

BELV, ABER and LBL are marked as having no traffic. Sites such as UCSB, BBN and NORSR appear in this list.
sections.eli5: Each row is one computer, with messages it sent elsewhere and messages it kept at home.

sections.title: What the Numbers Show
sections.content:
ISI HOST 1 again had the most internode packets of any single Host, 12941890, with a daily average of 417480. AMEST HOST 2 had 11474180 and AMES HOST 0 had 9256256. Some intranode counts are large, for example 23380090 at CCA HOST 0 and 11320100 at SRI HOST 0.

The totals are 83499220 internode and 58210780 intranode packets. The daily average is 2693523 and 1877767, the average per node-day is 72798 and 50750, and the packets-per-message figure for internode traffic is 1.04.
sections.eli5: A few busy computers sent most of the messages, and the report adds everything up at the bottom.
